lines.text: Try it. From the tools folder, run the replay tool with dash dash synthetic. It simulates one approach and writes a robot-style log.
Then it replays those photos through Tag Tracker and six other filter versions, and compares each one with the truth.
Compare more forgetting with the shipped filter. In our run, four times the drift made the estimate wobble about twice as much.
On the real robot, try the spin test. Turn in place at about one radian per second with a tag in view, and watch Tag Pose.
It should stay still. If it swings back and forth, the timestamps are off. If it traces a circle, the camera's mounting pose is off.
What's next? Collisions. A push that slides all four wheels together fools the wheel pose, so the tag's place is suddenly wrong.
In our simulator, a hard push near the target fooled the robot into a false done thirty two percent of the time.
The plan: compare the gyro chip's accelerometer with the wheels. In our simulator, that caught ninety five percent of skids. Not in the code yet.
After a skid, the robot would stop trusting its lock, back off thirty centimeters, and lock on again.
That's how a robot hits a two centimeter target. The lessons behind it are at f r c fifty seven twelve dot com.
